questions.key_step: Variance $np(1-p)$ gives $n=4$; then $P(X\ge2)=1-P(0)-P(1)$ since the mean is $1.6$.
questions.justification: Two routine formulas (variance, binomial pmf) and a complement; no decision beyond rounding the mean up to 2.

questions.key_step: Subtracting the two sums of squares gives $\sum x_i=40$ and $\sum x_i^2=180$; then $(6+k)^2+45=46$.
questions.justification: Four chained routine steps (sums, mean, variance, transformation law) ending in a quadratic; nothing unfamiliar.

questions.key_step: Cancel the $x$ coefficient to get $a=b$, then $\frac{\sqrt{1+x^2}-1}{x}=\tan\frac{\theta}{2}$ for $x=\tan\theta$ so $f=\frac12\tan^{-1}x$.
questions.justification: Series limit to find a, b plus a standard half-angle simplification before differentiating; two familiar tricks in sequence.

questions.key_step: No two odd digits adjacent: arrange the evens first and put the odds in the gaps, over three cases by number of odd digits.
questions.justification: Standard gap method with three cases; counts are small and options allow checking.

questions.key_step: The sum telescopes to $\tan^{-1}x$ (odd extension), and $\cos^{-1}\frac{1-x^2}{1+x^2}=2|\tan^{-1}x|$, so $f=3\tan^{-1}x$ for $x\ge0$ and $-\tan^{-1}x$ for $x<0$.
questions.justification: Telescoping tan^-1 series with branch care, then a piecewise function whose graph decides four statements (continuity, differentiability, extremum, solution counts). Two concepts, so the 2.5 floor applies but does not bind.

questions.key_step: Linear pmf $a+bk$: the two conditions $\sum p=1$, $E[X]=2$ give $a=b=\frac1{10}$; each statement is then a direct computation.
questions.justification: Two linear equations then four short routine evaluations (tail, variance, conditional probability, scaling law); nothing needs insight.

questions.key_step: $f=t\lfloor 1/t\rfloor$ with $t=\{x\}$ lies in $(1-t,1]$ so $f\to1$ at integers, yet $\frac{f(x)-1}{x}=-\{1/x\}$ oscillates; $g=\sin^2(\pi x)f$ kills the oscillation and keeps the jumps at $n+\frac1m$.
questions.justification: Four statements each needing a real check on a fractional-part/greatest-integer function: continuity by squeeze, non-differentiability by oscillation, differentiability of g, and equality of discontinuity sets. Several concepts so the 2.5 floor applies but does not bind.

questions.key_step: Complement of the union is the single colour order G,B,R; with $P(E_i)=\frac7{12}$ and symmetry of the pair intersections, inclusion-exclusion gives every statement.
questions.justification: Three overlapping events on sequential draws, four numerical statements each needing exact fractions; the symmetry insight shortens it but a slip in any fraction is costly.

questions.key_step: Gap method for (A) and (D), mirror-half for the palindrome (B), and inclusion-exclusion over three blocks for (C), which gives 1806, not 1890.
questions.justification: Four counting statements with repeated letters, each needing its own technique and exact arithmetic; (C) is a near-miss trap.

questions.key_step: $A_n=\binom{2n}{n}$ by Vandermonde, $B_n=nA_n-B_n$ by $r\to n-r$, and $r\binom nr=n\binom{n-1}{r-1}$ for $C_n$; the ratio then follows.
questions.justification: Three standard identities each needing a recognised trick, then comparison of expressions; every statement must be judged.

questions.key_step: Four short counting items: multinomial coefficient, gap method, combinations, divisibility by 3 by omitting digit 3.
questions.justification: Four independent routine counts, elimination possible from the options; typical matching level.

questions.key_step: Four direct textbook counts (equal groups, coin tosses, committee, non-consecutive pair).
questions.justification: Each item is a single standard formula or short count; options plus elimination make it easy.

questions.key_step: Expand $y$ as a power series $a_1x+a_2x^2+a_3x^3$ in the implicit relation and equate coefficients to get $a_3=\frac56$, so $f'''(0)=5$.
questions.justification: Implicit relation needing third-order information; series bookkeeping with several cross terms, no options to check.

questions.key_step: Continuity at 0 fixes $a=-1,b=-2$; roots then need an IVT plus a monotonicity proof, and on $(-2,0)$ the sign of $f'$ rests on $x\cos x-\sin x>0$.
questions.justification: Four stages (limit with trig, parameter values, root counting on two pieces) with a non-trivial derivative-sign argument on the left piece; a numerical answer with no options.

questions.key_step: Only $8k^3$ matters: floor and $k\ln(1+k/n)$ add $O(n^2)$, and $k^2\sin k=O(n^2)$ against $n^4$, so squeeze gives $\sum 8k^3/n^4\to2$.
questions.justification: Squeeze or Riemann-sum recognition with floor and sin perturbations; the idea is a known pattern but the bounding must be done carefully.

questions.key_step: Derivatives of the inverse at $f(0)=1$ need $f'(0)=3,f''(0)=1,f'''(0)=0$ and the formulas for $g'',g'''$; the combination gives $1-2+6=5$.
questions.justification: Third derivative of an inverse function is not a routinely memorised formula; the chain is mechanical but error-prone.

questions.key_step: $1^\infty$ form: $\ln f=\lim n(\text{base}-1)=1+\frac{x^4}{1-x^2}$ (the $x^2$ terms cancel); then series of numerator to the $x^8$ term gives $4$.
questions.justification: Two nested expansions (cube root of cosine in 1/n, then a series in x up to $x^8$) with cancellations; heavy precise computation with no options.

questions.key_step: Mean deviation about the mode $=\frac{10+k}{12+k}=\frac78$ gives $k=4$; then mean $3.375$ and mean deviation $\frac{59}{64}$.
questions.justification: Routine statistics formulas in sequence with fraction arithmetic; unique-mode condition is only a side check.
